bullets.title: AI trade surges: CRWV +14-19% on monster beat, OpenAI $10B quarter, TSMC 'insatiable' demand
bullets.body: CoreWeave Q3 revenue +168% YoY to $3.66B beat by ~300bps; raised FY26 revenue guide to $13.0-13.3B and adj. operating income +26%, with 4Q margins guided to ~16.5% vs 14.1% Street. OpenAI hit $10B quarterly revenue (+50% QoQ, ~$50B annualized run rate); TSMC called leading-edge chip demand 'insatiable.' Together these catalysts revived the AI infrastructure complex with SOXX +5%, memory stocks +6-8%, and S&P futures +0.84-0.87%.

bullets.title: CRWV financing fears resolved: $9B prepayments, no unsecured debt through 2027, renewals = $10B upside
bullets.body: CRWV secured ~$9B in customer prepayments over next 3 months, eliminating need for unsecured debt markets through 2027; 70% of deals collected prepayments and next DDTL expected to price at 7-7.5% yield with investment-grade rating. GPU pricing surged 25-35% QoQ with short-duration contracts commanding >$40M/MW vs. older $10-11M contracts; 2027-2028 renewals represent ~$10B in incremental annualized revenue with no additional capex. Demand is 10x available capacity through end-2027.

bullets.title: NVDA governance crisis: Baird downgrades to Neutral/$200 PT; CEO resignation calls mount despite +3.5-5% premarket bounce
bullets.body: Baird cut NVDA to Neutral from Outperform and slashed PT to $200 from $500 citing CEO Jensen Huang spy-scandal fallout and political pressure, while Citi trimmed PT 10% to $285. Senate Banking member called for Huang's resignation; Commerce Department reportedly delayed blacklisting Megaspeed despite agency pressure. NVDA's RSI hit 24 (lowest since 2019) but stock bounced 3.5-5.2% premarket on broader AI optimism, with Morgan Stanley dropping it from Top Pick under stop-loss while maintaining OW.

bullets.title: Fed trajectory hawkish: GS adds March 2027 hike; 10-year at 5.00%, December 50bp odds at 12-28%
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs added a third 25bp hike (March 2027) to its forecast following hotter October CPI (headline +0.35% MoM, core +0.30%). Markets are pricing 28bp odds of a 50bp December move per JPM, though 22V Research sees only 12% odds and maintains short VIX/long risk-on, arguing consumer slowdown will eventually enable Fed pivot. US 10-year note is at 5.00%, 2-year at 4.748%, with Asia sovereign yields rising sharply in sympathy.

bullets.title: SPX technically bullish: JPM targets 8,000 YE26 (+8.4%); semis near DeMark buy signal with 70% of SOX oversold
bullets.body: JPM's Dubravko reiterates YE26 SPX target of 8,000 ($365 EPS at 21.9x), implying 8.4% upside, noting AI upstream is an attractive entry point post-52% semi/60% memory compression from May peaks. Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shows 70% of constituents near DeMark buy signals vs. 36.67% last week. S&P implied equity risk premium sits at an unusually high 5%+, suggesting +11% upside if it reverts to 4.5%.

bullets.title: Semiconductor export controls tightening: US to close 'neocloud loophole'; Schumer pushing fast-track chip restrictions
bullets.body: Senate Democratic Leader Schumer is pushing quick approval of new US chip export restrictions to China; the US is also reportedly moving to close the 'neocloud loophole' that allowed Chinese AI companies to access advanced Nvidia GPUs through third-country cloud providers. The measures add geopolitical overhang on the AI infrastructure complex even as demand fundamentals remain robust.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO demand pushes implied valuation past $1.5T; TSMC to invest $500M each in ANT and OpenAI
bullets.body: Investor demand for the Anthropic IPO is so strong that perpetual futures signal a first-day pop with valuation discussions exceeding $1.5T. UBS and Jefferies are hosting investor education sessions. TSMC is reportedly planning $500M investments in both Anthropic and OpenAI, underscoring hyperscaler alignment with frontier AI labs.

bullets.title: Fed Governor Bowman warns of sharp equity correction if AI investment returns disappoint
bullets.body: Fed Governor Bowman flagged risk of a sharp equity correction if AI capex does not generate commensurate returns—a notable central bank caution on the AI buildout narrative. This comes as 22V Research and JPM both note that every $100B in hyperscaler capex translates to only ~$9 in SPX EPS impact (~2.5% earnings growth).

bullets.title: Optical and fiber names catching bid as AI risk-on signal; GLW initiated Buy at Jefferies ($134 PT)
bullets.body: Jefferies initiated Corning (GLW) at Buy with a $134 PT (20% upside) on fiber demand running ahead of supply with multi-year hyperscaler agreements; photonics inside the box is flagged as the next major opportunity from 2028. Optical names (LITE, COHR, CRDO, MTSI) showed early pre-market strength as a risk-on signal even as memory stocks remain down 20-25% over 10 days.

bullets.title: 3Q26 S&P earnings on track for 32% EPS growth; 77% beat rate, Big Tech lagging rest of market
bullets.body: With 81.6% of S&P 500 market cap reported, 3Q26 EPS is tracking +32% YoY with revenues +14.6%; 77% of companies are beating projections by 5.7% in aggregate. Big 6 Tech+ is lagging at 22.4% EPS growth vs. 35.3% for the rest of the index. Key upcoming prints: NVDA ($108.8B rev cons, Nov 17), CSCO ($18.1B, Nov 12), DIS ($25.2B, Nov 17).

bullets.title: Russell 2000 up 13.7% YTD, outperforming S&P by 3.8%; 76% market cap beat 3Q earnings by 7.8%
bullets.body: MS SMID-Cap notes the Russell 2000 is up 13.7% YTD vs. S&P 500, outperforming by 3.8%. 1,040 of Russell 2000 stocks (76% of market cap) reported 3Q26 earnings 7.8% above expectations. The small-cap complex fell 0.7% on Nov 10, underperforming SPX by 0.3%, on rate hike fears.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples compressed: IGV -9.5% YTD vs S&P +10.5%; All-SaaS at 5.4x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.4x FY+2 EV/Sales (down 6.24% WoW) while All-Security sits at 7.8x (down 10.77% WoW). IGV has returned -9.5% YTD vs. the S&P 500's +10.5%, reflecting significant multiple compression in software. Short interest remains elevated in unprofitable tech, with 70% of NDX and 75% of IGV closing lower on November 10.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce inflecting in 2027: AI retail traffic +130% YoY this holiday; AMZN, META, GOOGL positioned
bullets.body: Citi sees agentic commerce reaching inflection in 2027, with Adobe data showing AI-driven retail traffic growing 130% YoY this holiday vs. +4% for search and +17% for social; AI-referred shoppers convert ~48% better. AMZN (400M+ Alexa Shopping users), META (Muse at 4.4M DAUs), and GOOGL (AI Mode prompts 3x longer than traditional search) are best positioned, with consumer data/memory identified as the key competitive moat.

bullets.title: Oil -11% since last Tuesday on Iran peace deal expectations; crude at $86.64, Brent below $90
bullets.body: Crude oil fell 11% over the past week as expectations for an Iran peace deal mounted; Brent broke below $90 after Trump pulled back strike threats, with fair value seen at $80-85. The move is a potential tailwind for consumer discretionary and cyclicals, with Morgan Stanley noting discretionary median NTM P/E has re-rated to 18x from 16x but remains below 21x YE2025, still requiring earnings follow-through.

bullets.title: HF net leverage at 12-month lows; semis most net-sold; momentum crowding reset from 100th to 76th percentile
bullets.body: JP Morgan prime notes HF net leverage fell ~4% over the past week to 12-month lows with equity L/S net leverage at three-year lows; global momentum exposure is near three-year lows with semis remaining the most net-sold sector. AI positioning reset from 100th percentile to 76th percentile on momentum crowding, which JPM views as an attractive re-entry point for the AI upstream trade.

bullets.title: Hawkish CPI drove US 2-year biggest move since Apr-25; US bond market closed today (Veterans Day)
bullets.body: October CPI (headline +0.35% MoM, core +0.30%) triggered the largest US 2-year yield move since April 2025, pushing the 10-year to 5.00% and the 2-year to 4.748%. The US bond market is closed today for Veterans Day, limiting price discovery on rates, while equity futures are trading strongly higher on the AI narrative.

bullets.title: Geopolitical risks: Iran escalating nuclear rhetoric; Treasury Secretary relocated to military base
bullets.body: Iran is escalating rhetoric on nuclear material and potential strikes on US military bases; Treasury Secretary Bessent has been relocated to a military base due to Iranian security threats. Oil is falling on peace deal hopes, creating a cross-current with the military escalation headlines.

bullets.title: Wolfe DC Policy: Minimal legislation expected in 2027-28; credit card rate caps, AI regulation, clean energy blocked
bullets.body: Wolfe Research expects divided government to produce minimal legislative output: healthcare deals unlikely before late 2027, credit card rate caps and interchange fee legislation improbable despite Trump-Warren overlap, and AI regulation and clean energy policy not expected to advance. GS separately estimates a 10-18% credit card APR cap would create significant earnings pressure (36% cap implies ~2-3% EPS downside for major issuers).

bullets.title: TSMC capex to reach $90B/$109B in 2027/28; four new N3 fabs plus steep N2 ramp underway
bullets.body: JPM's chip analysis shows TSMC accelerating capacity 2-3x typical annual build with four new N3 fabs and a steep N2 ramp; capex expected at $90B in 2027 and $109B in 2028, with USD revenue growing 40%/28% YoY respectively. October TSMC revenue of NT$586.9B (+60% YoY, +15% MoM) is tracking to ~34% of 4Q consensus, pointing to mid-to-high end of guidance.

bullets.title: Citi retail card data: November starts weak at -3.0% YoY; Electronics +19% the lone bright spot
bullets.body: Citi credit card data for November week 1 shows total spending at -3.0% YoY (ex-food -2.7%), decelerating from -2.5% the prior week. Electronics surged +19% (4th consecutive week of strength), Jewelry +25.8%, and Cosmetics +4.6%, while Athletic Footwear crashed -31%, Apparel -22%, and Department Stores -12.2%. The data suggests a bifurcated consumer heading into the holiday season.
